title: Specify needs
description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options and preparing a business case, which may weigh the benefits of addressing these needs against expected costs, risks and other requirements, considering the public good arising from meeting those needs and the implications for respondents, users and other stakeholders. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The updated GSBPM description for 'Specify Needs' highlights that activities such as needs identification, stakeholder engagement, and business case formulation are now 'increasingly supported by automated and AI-powered processes,' aiming to 'minimize manual effort for routine or repetitive tasks and surface insights for human decision-makers.' This shift means EC-02 roles that historically involved stakeholder engagement, data gathering, researching, and initial analysis will now need to adapt to: (a) working closely with automated systems to synthesize needs and feedback; (b) validating and interpreting AI-generated insights; and (c) focusing less on manual gathering and more on expert contextualization. The 'Junior Evaluation Officer' role is directly implicated because the work-description states they 'conduct literature and data research, identify, gather, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data,' and 'provide input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' With automation handling more routine synthesis, this officer will need to shift toward high-value interpretation and oversight of AI-supported outputs: 'The incumbent is required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process; prepare statistical and narrative summaries for review...' They will be more involved in validating AI summaries, contextualizing input data, and making recommendations based on AI-driven drafts.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' role states they 'participate in the analysis of statistical program data and assist in the preparation of analytical material... for internal use and publication purposes' and 'suggest possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assist in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' The GSBPM update requires that these officers support AI-enabled consultation analysis and focus on strategic review and prioritization of needs surfaced by automated synthesis. Their responsibilities for analyzing feedback, preparing recommendations, and interpreting user needs are now less about manual collation and more about oversight, validation, and nuanced contextualization of AI findings. Their knowledge of data flows and evaluation techniques will be directed toward managing and supervising AI-driven inputs and focusing effort on the highest value-add problems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' role is affected by a shift to automation and AI-driven process automation in needs identification and documentation: 'Conducts data preparation techniques... ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' 'Supports the conduct of studies... using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods.' These analysts will now support digital/AI pipelines for needs analysis, validating outputs, and focusing on critical assessment, standardization, and deeper analysis instead of repetitive manual data gathering. The role's emphasis on 'data stewardship... to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use' remains, but more of their day-to-day will involve interacting with, tuning, and critically appraising AI outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Identify needs
description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. It may be triggered by a new information request from users, an environmental change such as a reduced budget, a periodic review, or respondent feedback. Action plans from evaluations of previous iterations of the production cycle (including from respondent feedback) or from other programmes might provide an input to this sub-process. It also includes consideration of practice amongst other (national and international) statistical organisations producing similar data and the methods used by those organisations.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The GSBPM update specifies that 'AI and automated tools are used to continuously scan for new information requests... and aggregate respondent feedback,' automating much of the initial investigation and identification. However, staff roles must now focus on interpreting, reviewing, and confirming needs synthesized by AI. The 'Junior Evaluation Officer' is implicated because they are responsible for 'conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data' and 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions.' With automated identification, their role transitions to expert oversight of AI-processed needs data, contextual interpretation, and strategic confirmation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' participates in 'the analysis of statistical program data,' 'suggests possible feedback on collection... and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' As needs investigation becomes automated, this role adapts from manual environmental scanning to 'assessing the validity of collected and processed data,' now largely in partnership with AI and automated feedback synthesis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' conducts data preparation techniques and supports studies/projects involving statistical data analysis. They now partner with automation in gathering and classifying needs data, maintaining emphasis on 'ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' but shifting toward validation and review of AI-generated synthesized needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Consult and confirm needs
description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with the internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. A good understanding of user needs is required so that the statistical organisation knows not only what it is expected to deliver, but also when, how, and perhaps most importantly, why. For the second and subsequent iterations of this sub-process, the main focus will be on determining whether previously identified needs have changed. This detailed understanding of user needs is the critical part of this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The update indicates that 'automated and AI-supported systems are now used to organize and analyze input from stakeholders,' while staff 'engage directly where nuanced negotiation, detailed interpretation, or complex prioritization is required.' The 'Junior Evaluation Officer,' who 'participates in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups, applying analytical tools,' and 'provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data,' is heavily implicated. Their skills in direct consultation now focus on high-value interpretation of stakeholder input and guiding strategic negotiation—overseeing, validating, and finalizing outputs from automated synthesis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' 'provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.' In the context of automated feedback organization, this becomes a quality and prioritization oversight role for stakeholder requirements, rather than a manual aggregator. The work-description's emphasis on 'liaising with subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate requirements' aligns with consulting and confirming needs with AI assistance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Establish output objectives
description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). It includes agreeing the suitability of the proposed outputs and their quality measures with users. Legal or normative frameworks (e.g. relating to confidentiality, methodologies), and available resources are important to consider when establishing output objectives.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: With the update, 'AI and automated tools aggregate and analyze confirmed user requirements... and generate draft output objectives.' Staff are tasked with oversight and finalization. The 'Junior Evaluation Officer' 'participates... to evaluate... performance' and 'provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions,' making them responsible for reviewing and confirming automated draft objectives, assessing quality, and contextualizing outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' role of providing 'analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations' is directly relevant. Their focus shifts to confirming appropriateness of AI-proposed output objectives, ensuring compliance with standards and legal requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Identify concepts
description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. At this stage, the concepts identified might not align with existing statistical standards. This alignment, and the choice or definition of the statistical and other concepts and variables to be used, takes place in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The update highlights two changes: (1) AI/automation supports 'synthesize user requirements, prior documentation, and relevant internal/external sources,' and (2) the 'subject matter sponsor is solely accountable' for final specification and certification. The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' must now validate AI-suggested concepts and is accountable for final specification, as the work-description specifies knowledge of 'statistical or economic theory and principles... and methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation...' and liaising to 'develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development.' Their responsibilities now heavily involve overseeing AI-supported proposals, certifying their validity, and documenting concept definition for downstream design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Check data availability and suitability
description: This sub-process checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. An assessment of possible alternatives would normally include research into potential administrative or other non-statistical sources of data (e.g. privately-held data or “Big Data”), to: Determine whether they would be suitable for use for statistical purposes (e.g. the extent to which administrative concepts match data requirements, and whether the timeliness and quality of the data, security, and continuity of data supply are suitable); Assess the division of responsibilities between data suppliers and the statistical organisation; Check necessary ICT resources (e.g. data storage, technology required to handle incoming data and data processing) as well as any provision agreements with data suppliers (which could be legal or other agreements such as memoranda of understanding) for accessing and sharing the data (e.g. formats, delivery, accompanying metadata and quality check). When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: With the update, the process must now 'formalize a strict hierarchy of data sourcing—first considering existing data holdings, then administrative and alternative data, and only lastly, new survey data collection.' Further, the 'subject matter sponsor holds sole accountability,' and a 'center of expertise works collaboratively.' The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' is deeply implicated, as their work-description emphasizes assessing the 'validity of collected and processed data,' and 'analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' They must now systematically evaluate automated outputs about available data sources, certify the thoroughness and suitability, and partner with the designated data acquisition teams.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is implicated because the updated process requires staff who can 'validate AI/automation-enabled checks of data source quality, timeliness, and coverage,' and 'propose improvements and alternatives for data acquisition.' Their work-description specifies 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling...' and 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies...' Reinforcing a move to digital-first, automated sourcing, they will be required to focus on the technical assessment and validation of new (especially automated or alternative) data source quality and suitability.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Prepare and submit business case
description: This sub-process documents the findings of the other sub-processes in this phase, in the form of a business case to get approval to implement the new or modified statistical business process. Such a business case would need to conform to the requirements of the approval body, but would typically include elements such as: A description of the “As-Is” business process (if it already exists), with information on how the current statistics are produced, highlighting any inefficiencies and issues to be addressed; The proposed “To-Be” solution, detailing how the statistical business process will be developed to produce the new or revised statistics; An assessment of costs and benefits against objectives and any external constraints. The business case describes options and makes recommendations. It may include the benefits, costs, deliverables, time frame, budget, required technical and human resources, risk assessment and impact on stakeholders for each option. After the business case is prepared, it is submitted for approval to move to the next phase of the business process. At this sub-process, a “go”/“no go” decision is made. Typically, the business case is reviewed and formally approved or disapproved by the appropriate sponsors and governance committees.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The GSBPM update states 'automated and AI-driven systems are used to collate, analyze, and generate initial drafts for all key business case sections.' Staff now review, contextualize, and refine these drafts. The 'Junior Evaluation Officer,' whose work-description specifies 'provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management on elements of program evaluations of various programs,' and 'conducts analyses and interpretation of data collected during evaluation studies under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager,' is now focused on critically reviewing, supplementing, and validating drafted business case materials produced by automation, ensuring they are strategically sound for decision making.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' is implicated as their role includes 'providing data and assistance to users... participates in the analysis of data... and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.' As AI/automation assembles business case materials, their expertise enables strategic review—ensuring all options, risks, and contextual implications are properly articulated and substantiated.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Design
description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments and operational processes, with due regard to other requirements such as security. It includes all the design elements needed to define or refine the statistical products or services identified in the business case. This phase specifies all relevant metadata, in accordance with the standards and corporate policies, ready for use later in the business process, as well as quality assurance procedures. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration and whenever improvement actions are identified in the Evaluate phase of a previous iteration. Design activities make substantial use of international and national standards in order to reduce the length and cost of the design process, and enhance interoperability, comparability, etc. Organisations may reuse or adapt design elements from existing processes and consider geospatial aspects of data in the design to enhance the usability and value of the statistical information. Additionally, outputs of design processes may form the basis for future standards at the organisational, national or international levels. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The phase now requires 'automation and AI' for drafting, standards synthesis, metadata creation, and versioning; all outputs must be 'richly described, and machine-actionable,' and staff must be adept at reviewing and contextualizing automated design outputs. The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer' is core to this, as their work includes 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata,' and 'provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata.' Their work will now focus less on manual documentation/metadata production and more on reviewing, adapting, and improving AI/automation-generated metadata and outputs, driving digital transformation and interoperability.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is required to have 'knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence...' and 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation.' With the Design phase now shifting to automation for specification, standards compliance, and output configuration, they shift toward validating, quality assuring, and contextualizing AI/automation-generated component and system designs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' is implicated through 'analysis of data and assistance in the preparation of analytical material,' and 'suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods.' With digital-first and standardization the norm, they focus on the review, strategic selection, and adaptation of standards-embedded designs and automated metadata outputs—for both methodological integrity and fit-for-purpose analytical use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Design outputs and dissemination
description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including the related systems, tools and procedures used in the Disseminate phase. Processes governing access to any confidential outputs are also designed here. Outputs should be designed to follow existing standards wherever possible, so inputs to this process may include metadata from similar or previous collections (including extractions from statistical, administrative, geospatial and other non-statistical registers and databases), international standards, and information about practices in other statistical organisations from sub-process 1.1 (Identify needs). Outputs may also be designed in partnership with other interested bodies, particularly if they are considered to be joint outputs, or they will be disseminated by another organisation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Digital automation, standards, and metadata-rich, machine-actionable products are now required. The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer''s focus on 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata,' as well as contributing to 'documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals,' is reoriented toward the oversight of automation-driven, standards-based design outputs, ensuring discoverability, API compatibility, and proper metadata linkage in digital dissemination environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' is implicated because they 'edit, validate, market, and disseminate data,' 'review and assess data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases,' and 'interpret client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.' As output and dissemination design is automated and standardized, this officer will focus on QA, metadata validation, and supporting fit-for-purpose output design—including selection/omission of visualization types—ensuring robust machine-actionability and user-centered dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Design variables
description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as any other variables that will be derived from them in sub-process 5.5 (Derive new variables and units), and any statistical or geospatial classifications that will be used. This is also where unit types (including observation units and statistical units) can be designed. It is expected that existing national and international standards will be followed wherever possible. This sub-process may need to run in parallel with sub-process 2.3 (Design collection), as the definition of the variables to be collected and the choice of collection instruments may be inter-dependent to some degree. Preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, statistical and geospatial classification is a necessary precondition for subsequent phases.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The need for 'full standards compliance (SDMX and prescribed tools),' 'AI/LLM-enabled tooling for the automated generation, refinement, and validation of variable descriptions and attributes,' and staff 'proficiency in digital metadata standards and tooling' puts the 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer' in a central position: 'prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata,' and 'assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations.' The officer's expertise is now directed at supervising AI generation of variable descriptions and ensuring standards and metadata completeness in digital repositories, and documenting/validating digital variable management.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also implicated—'knowledge of data science and its life cycle... warehousing, cleansing, processing, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization' and 'conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation.' These skills adapt toward validation and enrichment of AI/LLM-derived variable sets, focusing on compliance and interoperability, and technical validation within modern metadata management systems.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Design collection
description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data, and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, which may depend on the type of data collection, the collection unit type (enterprise, person, or other) and the available sources of data. The actual activities in this sub-process will vary according to the type of collection instrument required, which can include computer assisted interviewing, paper questionnaires, administrative registers, automated and semi-automated data transfer methods (such as using APIs, machine-to-machine integrations and various types of file transfers), web-scraping technologies as well as technology for geospatial data. The collection may employ a multi-mode method which requires additional considerations such as design of sequencing or different instruments for different modes. Direct or indirect use of administrative data may be introduced in the data collection mode for either controlling survey data or assisting it when capturing survey information. In the case of survey (or census) data, this collection strategy includes the design of the collection instruments, questions and response templates (in conjunction with the variables and statistical classifications designed in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables)). It is important to understand respondents and incorporate the user perspectives in the design of data collection. This sub-process may include design of fieldwork operations, and respondent engagement, in the case of survey data collection. It also includes the confirmation of existing agreements or creation of new agreements. This sub-process is enabled by tools such as question libraries (to facilitate the reuse of questions and related attributes), questionnaire tools (to enable the quick and easy compilation of questions into formats suitable for cognitive testing) and agreement templates (to help standardise terms and conditions). This sub-process also includes the design of respondent management systems that are specific to this business process. Where statistical organisations do not collect data directly (i.e. a third party controls the collection and processing of the data), this sub-process may include the design of mechanisms to monitor the data and the metadata to assess impacts of any change made by the third party.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Now that collection design must 'prioritize passive, administrative, and already-available sources of data,' and automate 'design, rendering, and fielding' using AI where surveys are required, the 'Operations Officer' is critical: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' 'evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.' Their work will change as routine strategy and operational design become increasingly automated. The officer is more focused on ensuring collection design incorporates these new priorities for automation, digital integration (APIs, passive sources), and compliance with passive-first policies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also involved, with skills in 'data capture and acquisition, data extraction... processing...' and 'knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies...' Their work will now emphasize vetting, QA, and technical support for automated, digital-first collection system designs (including passive acquisition, APIs, AI-driven survey logic/design).
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Design frame and sample
description: This sub-process applies especially to processes which involve data collection based on sampling, such as through statistical surveys, but it may also apply to other types of data collection such as census or register-based (e.g., filtering of registers based on the target population). It identifies and specifies the population of interest, defines a sampling frame (and, where necessary, the register from which it is derived), and determines the most appropriate sampling criteria and methodology (which could include complete enumeration). Common sources for a sampling frame are administrative and statistical registers, censuses and information from other sample surveys. It may refer to geospatial data and classifications. This sub-process describes how these sources can be combined if needed. Analysis of whether the frame covers the target population should be performed. Spatial analysis techniques can be used to ensure the spatial distribution of the units is appropriate. A sampling plan should be made. The actual sample is created in sub-process 4.1 (Create frame and select sample), using the methodology specified in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The update requires the adoption of 'AI-driven data cleaning and pre-processing by partners,' 'full integration with end-to-end digital pipelines,' and options for 'person-based and adaptive sampling.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' is implicated, as they are familiar with 'data preparation techniques..., data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' and participate 'in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.' Their technical role expands into the QA and supervision of AI-enabled and partner-prepared frames, oversight for integration into digital workflows, and adoption/support of flexible sampling designs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Operations Officer' 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations'; the knowledge areas cited include the 'concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities.' As sampling designs must now support 'dynamic and flexible options (including person-based),' and as pipeline integration is prioritized, their practical, systems-based knowledge and focus on operational feasibility and integration is increasingly central.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Design processing and analysis
description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases. This can include, among others, specification of routines and rules for coding, editing and imputation, which may vary based on the means of data collection and source of data. This subprocess also includes design of specifications for data integration from multiple data sources, validation of data and estimation. Statistical disclosure control methods are also designed here if they are specific to this business process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The sub-process now requires 'automation, AI/ML-driven tools' for coding, imputation, validation, integration, and estimation, and mandates usage of standards (SDMX, .STAT, prescribed tools). The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with 'knowledge of data science..., data cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting...'—will now focus on implementing, reviewing, documenting, and testing automated/AI-driven analytical routines and ensuring complete digital traceability and standards compliance.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' is also implicated for a similar reason: they have 'knowledge of methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling,' and 'evaluate and propose changes to processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods.' Their responsibilities expand into the oversight of AI-implemented methodologies, reviewing digital pipelines for theoretical rigor and ensuring all analysis routines are standards-compliant by design.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Design production systems and workflows
description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, taking an overview of all the processes required within the whole production process and ensuring that they fit together efficiently with no gaps or redundancies. Various systems and databases may be needed throughout the process. The GSBPM can be used to design a statistical organisation’s business architecture layer when a statistical organisation has an existing enterprise architecture in place. The design might be adjusted to fit the organisation. A general principle is to reuse processes and technology across many statistical business processes, so existing production solutions (e.g. services, systems and databases) should be examined first, to determine whether they are fit for purpose for this specific production process, then, if any gaps are identified, new solutions can be designed. This sub-process also considers how staff will interact with systems and who will be responsible for what and when.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: With 'modular, event-driven, and AI-enabled workflows for the entirety of the statistical production process' now a requirement, the 'Operations Officer'—responsible for 'participating in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' and for 'analyzing and preparing reports for program managers... problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives'—must now prioritize automation, modularity, and reusability in designing systems and workflows, as well as ongoing operational quality assurance under highly automated, digitally orchestrated settings.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is expected to support and validate 'modular, automation-ready, and event-driven digital pipelines,' ensuring end-to-end system integrity and smooth transitions between all process phases. Their technical skills, knowledge of workflow configuration, and partnership on 'project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis' will now be directed toward the implementation and refinement of digital-first, inter-operable workflows across the statistic production lifecycle.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Build
description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the 'live' environment. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured in this phase to create the complete operational environment to run the process. New services are built by exception, created in response to gaps in the existing catalogue of services sourced from within the organisation and externally. These new services are constructed to be broadly reusable in alignment with the business architecture of the organisation where possible, and compliant with security requirements. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration, following a review or a change in methodology or technology, rather than for every iteration. The Build phase is broken down into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases. The first three sub-processes are concerned with the development and improvement of systems used in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data. The last four subprocesses focus on the end-to-end process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The GSBPM update for the Build phase emphasizes 'modular automation and AI-driven assembly at every step,' with automated configuration, integration, and self-testing prioritized. The 'Operations Officer' plays a central role, as their responsibilities include 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.' Now, the officer's focus will be on validating, supervising, and adapting increasingly automated, digital system assemblies and integrations, ensuring proper configuration and compliance with automation-first practices.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' is also implicated, due to their technical activities with 'data preparation techniques,' system configuration, 'data validation,' and support of studies/projects involving data analysis and processing. As automation is prioritized for assembling and configuring production environments, their work will focus on QA, troubleshooting exceptions, and overseeing the real-time integration and deployment of automated components and data flows.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Reuse or build collection instruments
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase. The collection instruments are built based on the design specifications created during the Design phase. A collection may use one or more collection instruments to receive the data (e.g. personal or telephone interviews; paper, electronic or web questionnaires; SDMX web services). Collection instruments may also be data extraction routines used to gather data from existing statistical or administrative registers (e.g. by using existing service interfaces). This sub-process also includes preparing and testing the contents and functioning of that collection instrument (e.g. cognitive testing of the questions in a questionnaire). It is recommended to consider the direct connection of collection instruments to a metadata system, so that metadata can be more easily captured in the collection phase. Connecting metadata and data at the point of capture can save work in later phases. Capturing the metrics of data collection (paradata) is also an important consideration in this sub-process for calculating and analysing process quality indicators.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Updates require the 'subject matter sponsor' to be solely responsible for specification and certification of collection instruments, and a 'single designated centre' to handle their rendering using AI/automation. The 'Operations Officer', whose key activities include 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data,' and providing 'assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding', will be primarily focused on the operational aspect—implementing, adapting, and supporting the transition to single-centre, AI-driven rapid instrument creation and enforcing timeline and automation policies. Their knowledge of both manual and digital collection processes will be crucial for ensuring compliance, quality, and timely instrument delivery.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new components needed for the Process and Analyse phases, as designed in the Design phase. Services (re-)used may include dashboard functions and features, information services, transformation functions, geospatial data services, workflow management tools, respondent and metadata management services.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: GSBPM updates require all components to be 'built or retrofitted for automation, event-driven orchestration, and plug-and-play integration.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' is responsible for supporting 'data preparation techniques,' 'organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies,' and participates in teams for 'data management, research and analysis.' They will need to validate, configure, and ensure technical interoperability of AI/automation-ready analytical and processing modules, testing outputs and troubleshooting integration issues.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Reuse or build dissemination components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new components or reuse existing components needed for the dissemination of statistical products as designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination). All types of dissemination components are included, from those that produce traditional paper publications to those that provide web services, (linked) open data outputs, geospatial statistics, maps, or access to microdata.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The GSBPM update implies dissemination modules must be 'modular, API-enabled, and designed to support automated production and update of data tables, microsites, APIs, and open data endpoints.' The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' role includes 'edits, validates, markets and disseminates data,' and 'reviews and assesses data quality,' and 'participates on data production and dissemination teams.' Their job is now more focused on automation-based, QA-centric, and technical oversight of dissemination component builds and upgrades, ensuring standards, interoperability, automation compatibility, and effectiveness of delivery channels.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Configure workflows
description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems and transformations used within the business processes, from data collection through to dissemination. In this sub-process, the workflows are configured based on the design created in sub-process 2.6 (Design production systems and workflows). This could include modifying a standardised workflow for a specific purpose, assembling the workflows for the different phases together (possibly with a workflow/business process management system) and configuring systems accordingly.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Configuration must now focus on 'full automation, AI-powered orchestration and monitoring, seamless modular integration,' and 'real-time responsive data movement.' The 'Operations Officer' is implicated, as their traditional involvement in 'designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases' is now shaped by digital configuration and orchestration tools. They ensure that workflow configuration achieves compatibility with modern automation standards, supports effective exception management, and enables real-time responsiveness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' also plays a part by testing, validating, and advising on digital workflow configuration to support seamless transitions throughout the statistical pipeline. Their technical familiarity with data and process management translates into assisting pipeline monitoring, identifying inefficiencies, and ensuring workflows are correctly parameterized for automation and rapid response.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Test production systems
description: This sub-process is concerned with the testing of assembled and configured services and related workflows. It includes technical testing and sign-off of new programmes and routines, as well as confirmation that existing routines from other statistical business processes are suitable for use in this case. Whilst part of this activity concerning the testing of individual components and services could logically be linked with sub-processes 3.1 (Reuse or build collection instruments), 3.2 (Reuse or build processing and analysis components) and 3.3 (Reuse or build dissemination components), this sub-process also includes testing of interactions between assembled and configured services and ensuring that the whole production solution works in a coherent way. It can also include arranging secure channels for the transmission of the data, checking detailed information about files and metadata with a data supplier and receiving test files to assess if data are fit for use.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: With 'AI-powered self-testing, regression suites, and system audits' being standard, the 'Operations Officer' who 'analyses and prepares reports... on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives,' will now focus on analysis of automated test results, escalation of issues, and high-level oversight of automated go-live decisions—moving away from manual testing toward process supervision.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Test statistical business process
description: This sub-process describes the activities to manage a field test or pilot of the statistical business process. Typically, it includes a small-scale data collection, to test the collection instruments, followed by processing and analysis of the collected data, to ensure the statistical business process performs as expected. Following the pilot, it may be necessary to go back to a previous step and make adjustments to collection instruments, systems or components. For a major statistical business process, e.g. a population census, there may be several iterations until the process is working satisfactorily.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: AI-driven orchestration, monitoring, and iterative analysis of pilot runs are now emphasized. The 'Operations Officer' ('analyzes reported data and work results and prepares reports... on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered, recommending alternatives') will supervise digital pilot execution, review AI-generated monitoring reports, escalate significant process failures, and support design iteration based on pilot results.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Finalise production systems
description: This sub-process includes the activities to put the assembled and configured processes and services, including modified and newly-created services, into production ready for use. The activities include: Producing documentation about the process components, including technical documentation and user manuals; Training the users of the system on how to operate the process; Moving the process components into the production environment and ensuring they work as expected in that environment (this activity may also be part of sub-process 3.5 (Test production systems).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: GSBPM updates require 'automated deployment, digital documentation, and AI-assisted user onboarding/training.' The 'Operations Officer', whose tasks include 'writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery,' will now be responsible for reviewing and supplementing automated system documentation, facilitating digital onboarding, and overseeing the automated move to production. Their expertise is essential for validation and compliance review.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Collect
description: This phase collects or gathers all necessary information (e.g. data, metadata and paradata), using different collection approaches (e.g. acquisition, collection, extraction, transfer), and loads them into the appropriate environment for further processing. Whilst it can include validation of data set formats, it does not include any transformations of the data themselves, as these are all done in the Process phase. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The Collect phase is broken down into four sub-processes (Figure 10), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The updated GSBPM stresses digital orchestration, automation, and AI support for data intake, making passive data acquisition (administrative, digital, automated feeds) the default. The 'Operations Officer'—who 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data' and 'provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding'—will shift from hands-on manual or operational collection to oversight, troubleshooting, exception handling, and continuous improvement of digitalized and automated collection systems. They will need to validate that automation is functioning correctly, investigate exceptions, and ensure compliance with new passive-oriented approaches.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Create frame and select sample
description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). It also includes the coordination of samples between instances of the same business process (e.g. to manage overlap or rotation), and between different processes using a common frame or register (e.g. to manage overlap or to spread response burden). Quality assurance and approval of the frame and the selected sample are also undertaken in this sub-process, though maintenance of underlying registers, from which frames for several statistical business processes are drawn, is treated as a separate activity. The sampling aspect of this sub-process is often not relevant for processes based entirely on the use of preexisting sources (e.g. administrative sources and other non-survey sources) as such processes generally create frames from the available data and then follow a census approach. Variables from administrative and other non-statistical sources of data can be used as auxiliary variables in the construction of sampling design.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The GSBPM update requires use of AI/LLM tools for 'record linkage, deduplication, and harmonization across administrative, alternative, and legacy data sources,' improving frame quality. The 'Junior Data Analyst'—with responsibilities for 'data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin'—will primarily validate, QA, and interpret automated frame construction outputs. They will address edge cases, support harmonization efforts, and oversee the integrity of sampling frames generated or enhanced by automation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Set up collection
description: This sub-process ensures that the people, processes and technology (e.g. web-based applications, devices to be used in collection, communication channels) are ready to collect data and metadata, as designed. It takes place over a period of time, as it includes the strategy, planning and training activities in preparation for the specific instance of the statistical business process. Where the process is repeated regularly, some (or all) of these activities may not be explicitly required for each iteration. For one-off and new processes, these activities can be lengthy. For survey data, this sub-process includes: Training collection staff; Training system using supervised machine learning techniques; Ensuring collection resources are available (e.g. collection devices, apps, APIs); Agreeing on terms with any intermediate collection bodies, (e.g. sub-contractors for computer assisted telephone interviewing, web service providers); Configuring collection systems to request and receive the data, including location data; Ensuring the security of data to be collected; Preparing collection instruments (e.g. printing questionnaires, pre-filling them with existing data, loading questionnaires and data onto interviewers' devices/computers, APIs, web scraping tools); Providing information for respondents (e.g. drafting letters/emails to respondents, credentials, guidance or tailored information to address questions they may have, or notifying respondents when online reporting instruments will be made available); Translation of materials (e.g. into the different languages spoken or used in the country). For non-survey sources, this sub-process ensures that the necessary processes, systems and confidentiality procedures are in place, to receive or extract the necessary information from the source. This includes: Evaluating requests to obtain the data and logging the request in a centralised inventory; Initiating contacts with organisations providing the data, and sending an introductory package with details on the process of obtaining the data; Routine checks that the system is working as expected.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The sub-process now requires 'routine use of automation for recurring data acquisitions and ingestion partnerships,' 'minimum metadata standards,' and support for a 'one workforce' model. The 'Operations Officer' role is emphasized because it includes 'participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of... automated operations,' 'prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems,' and 'provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.' Now, their tasks will focus on: ensuring automated and AI-enabled systems are properly set up, verifying compliance with metadata standards, participating in flexible workforce allocation, and supporting training/resource adaptation for dynamic, digital-first environments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Run collection
description: This sub-process is where the collection is implemented. The different collection instruments are used to collect or gather the information, which may include raw microdata or aggregates produced at the source, as well as any associated metadata. For survey or census data, it can include: Initial contact with respondents to request data and any subsequent follow-up or reminder actions, recording when and how they were contacted, and whether they have reacted; Management of the relationship between the statistical organisation and respondents, so that it remains positive, and recording and responding to comments, queries and complaints. (Minimisation of the number of non-respondents contributes significantly to higher quality of the collected data.); Manual data entry at the point of contact, or fieldwork management, depending on the source and collection approach; Georeferencing at the same time as collection of the data (using inputs from location-enabled systems such as GPS), or recording location by putting a mark on a map, etc., depending on the geographical frame and the technology used. Automated logical checks on data at the point of collection (i.e. validation-on-entry for survey response data) are considered to take place in 5.3 (Review and validate). For administrative, geospatial, or other non-statistical data, the data supplier either sends it as scheduled or is contacted to send the information, which might require follow-ups. Broader technical-level engagement with data suppliers falls under the Data Supplier Management overarching activity. In the case where the data are published under an Open Data license and exist in machine-readable form, they may be freely accessed and used. This sub-process may also include the monitoring of data collection and making any necessary changes to improve data quality. This includes generating reports, visualising and adjusting the process for obtaining data to ensure the data are fit for use. When the collection meets its targets, it is closed and a report on the collection is produced. Some basic checks of the structure and integrity of the information received may take place within this sub-process, (e.g. checking that files are in the right format and contain the expected fields).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This sub-process must now provide 'AI-driven, real-time case management, workload balancing, and dynamic reallocation of resources,' prioritizing passive, automated data acquisition. The 'Operations Officer'—trained in both manual and automated system operation—will oversee deployment, monitor performance, support collection optimization through AI/automation dashboards, and engage in exception resolution and efficiency review. Their role is more supervisory, adaptive, and quality-focused, minimizing hands-on manual work in favor of digital oversight.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Operations Officer

title: Finalise collection
description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing. It may include manual or automatic data capture, for example, using clerical staff or optical character recognition tools to extract information from paper questionnaires, or converting the formats of files or encoding the variables received from other organisations. It may also include analysis of the metadata and paradata associated with collection to ensure the collection activities have met requirements. In cases where there is a physical collection instrument, such as a paper questionnaire, which is not needed for further processing, this sub-process manages the archiving of that material. When the collection instrument uses software such as an API or an app, this sub-process also includes the versioning and archiving of these. The data could be pseudonymised at this stage before further processing.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Collection finalization must now feature 'automated and AI/ML routines for validating and enriching metadata,' operate as an 'iterative, innovation-driven step,' and assign the subject matter sponsor as responsible for certification/acceptance. The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer'—who is responsible for 'preparing, editing, validating and disseminating statistical metadata,' 'providing input to reports for clients and management,' and 'compiling information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata'—will now handle/validate automated QA and AI-enriched metadata at finalization, advise on iterative improvements, and oversee digital processes for collection certification. Their domain expertise now shifts even more toward review, innovation recommendations, and improving automated QA effectiveness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Process
description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis. It is made up of sub-processes that integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data, so that they can be analysed and disseminated as statistical outputs. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The sub-processes in this phase can apply to data from both statistical and non-statistical sources (with the possible exception of sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights), which is usually specific to survey data). Some variables could be processed prior to others if they are required for data integration (e.g., geospatial variables if used for that purpose). The Process and Analyse phases can be iterative and parallel. Analysis can reveal a broader understanding of the data, which might make it apparent that additional processing is needed. Sometimes the estimates being processed might be already published aggregates (undertaken according to a Revision Policy). Activities within the Process and Analyse phases may also commence before the Collect phase is completed. This enables the compilation of provisional results where timeliness is an important concern for users, and increases the time available for analysis. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The updated GSBPM specifies that all data processing—integrating, classifying, checking, cleaning, and transforming—is now implemented 'via modular, version-controlled, automation- and AI/ML-enabled digital workflows.' The 'Junior Data Analyst,' who has responsibility for 'data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin,' is now required to oversee, validate, and continuously improve these automated pipelines. Instead of manually executing bulk processing, the analyst's role is expert oversight of automated outputs, exception handling, and process enhancement.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Integrate data
description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources. It is where the results of subprocesses in the Collect phase are combined. The input data can be from a mixture of external or internal sources, and a variety of collection instruments, including extracts of administrative and other non-statistical data sources. Administrative data or other non-statistical sources of data can substitute for all or some of the variables directly collected from a survey. This sub-process also includes harmonising or creating new figures that agree between sources of data. The result is a consolidated set of data.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: GSBPM updates mandate 'automated, AI/LLM-powered routines for record linking, harmonization, and consolidation.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' (responsible for 'data extraction, cleansing, transformation, validation') must supervise integration automation, review quality and completeness of resulting datasets, and handle exceptions where automated harmonization routines surface potential inconsistencies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Classify and code
description: This sub-process classifies and codes the input data. For example, automatic (or clerical) coding routines may assign numeric codes to text responses according to a pre-determined statistical classification to facilitate data capture and processing. Some questions have coded response categories on the questionnaires or administrative source of data, others are coded after collection using an automated process (which may apply machine learning or artificial intelligence techniques) or an interactive, manual process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The sub-process must now use event-driven, SDMX-standard automation and AI/LLM models for code/classification assignment. The 'Junior Data Analyst'—who has responsibility for 'data preparation techniques,' and 'data validation'—now configures, validates, and QAs the code/classification automation, ensuring ambiguous cases are properly routed for expert review and maintaining the accuracy and standards-compliance of all assignments.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Review and validate
description: This sub-process examines data to identify potential problems, errors and discrepancies such as outliers, item non-response, miscoding and duplicate records. It can also be referred to as input data validation. It may be run iteratively, validating data against pre-defined edit rules, usually in a set order. It may flag data for automatic or manual inspection or editing. Reviewing and validating can apply to data from any type of source, before and after integration, as well as imputed data from sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute). Whilst validation is treated as part of the Process phase, in practice, some elements of validation may occur alongside collection activities, particularly for approaches such as computer assisted collection. Whilst this sub-process is concerned with detection and localisation of actual or potential errors, any correction activities that actually change the data is done in sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: GSBPM now states 'modular, automated digital tools and AI/LLM-enabled validation routines' complete most review/validation of data. The 'Junior Data Analyst' will interpret reports/data flagged by automation, respond to complex or systemic anomalies, adjust quality assurance logic as required, and ensure audit trails are properly maintained.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Edit and impute
description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, new values may be inserted, or erroneous data may be removed in this sub-process. The terms editing and imputation cover a variety of methods to do this, often using a rule-based approach. Specific steps typically include: Determining whether to add or change data; Selecting the method to be used; Adding/changing data values; Writing the new data values back to the data set, and flagging them as changed; Producing metadata on the editing and imputation process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Updates require 'automated, modular, and AI/LLM-powered digital pipelines' for edit/impute. The 'Junior Data Analyst' provides oversight, QA, and review, manages audit trails for automated edits, and intervenes in novel/imputed records that cannot be resolved by automation, preserving data integrity.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Derive new variables and units
description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units that are not explicitly provided in the collection, but are needed to deliver the required outputs. It derives new variables by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables that are already present in the dataset, or applying different model assumptions. This activity may need to be iterative, as some derived variables may themselves be based on other derived variables. It is therefore important to ensure that variables are derived in the correct order. New units may be derived by aggregating or splitting data for collection units, or by various other estimation methods. Examples include deriving households where the collection units are persons or enterprises where the collection units are legal units.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Derivations must be 'modular, automation- and AI-powered.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' ensures auditability, reviews and validates derived variable/unit outputs for accuracy, flags exceptions, and ensures templates/logic are up to date.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Calculate weights
description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records according to the methodology developed in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). For example, weights can be used to 'gross-up' data to make them representative of the target population (e.g. for sample surveys or extracts of scanner data), or to adjust for non-response in total enumerations. In other situations, variables may need weighting for normalisation purposes. It may also include weight correction for benchmarking indicators (e.g. known population totals).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Automated, algorithm-driven, documented weighting is now the norm, with staff 'intervene when innovative methods, unexpected results, or diagnostic reviews are needed.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' oversees weight pipeline QA and interpretation, audits methods/output, and manages escalation as needed.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Calculate aggregates
description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. It includes summing data for records sharing certain characteristics (e.g. aggregation of data by demographic or geographic classifications), determining measures of average and dispersion, and applying weights from sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights) to derive appropriate totals. In the case of statistical outputs which use sample surveys, sampling errors corresponding to relevant aggregates may also be calculated in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: All aggregation now runs through 'modular, digital automation pipelines.' The 'Junior Data Analyst' enforces process/documentation standards, validates summary outputs, and supports innovation in calculation methods where required.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Finalise data files
description: This sub-process brings together the results of the other sub-processes in this phase in a data set (either micro- or macro-data), which is used as the input to the Analyse phase. Sometimes, this may be an intermediate rather than a final data set, particularly for business processes where there are strong time pressures, and a requirement to produce both preliminary and final estimates.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: GSBPM requires finalized datasets to meet 'standards for machine-readability, open formats, full documentation, and auditability.' The 'Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer' ('prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata') is responsible for ensuring standards, metadata completeness, QA, and supporting digital hand-off and deployment.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Junior Data Analyst' supports the technical aspects of dataset finalization, verifying dataset quality, audit trails, metadata, and open format compliance, and liaising with next-phase users.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst

title: Analyse
description: In this phase, statistical outputs are produced and examined in detail. It includes preparing statistical content (including commentary, technical notes, etc.), and ensuring outputs are “fit for purpose” prior to dissemination to users. This phase also includes the sub-processes and activities that enable statistical analysts to understand the data and the statistics produced. The outputs of this phase could also be used as an input to other sub-processes (e.g. analysis of new sources as input to the Design phase). For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in every iteration. The Analyse phase and sub-processes are generic for all statistical outputs, regardless of how the data were sourced. The Analyse phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 12), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: GSBPM updates require 'automated, AI-powered, and modular analytical pipelines' for output creation and validation, with human analysts focusing on contextualization, interpretation, and communicating nuanced findings. The 'Economist/Sociologist 2', whose work includes 'participates in the analysis of statistical program data,' 'assists in the preparation of analytical material,' and 'identifies statistical trends and developments,' will increasingly oversee, review, and contextualize AI-generated analyses rather than perform manual computation. They will focus on providing advanced subject-matter interpretation, tailoring output explanations for users, and innovating in analytic commentary.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

title: Prepare draft outputs
description: This sub-process is where the data from sub-processes 5.7 (Calculate aggregates) and 5.8 (Finalise data files) are transformed into statistical outputs, which could include indexes, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, microdata, etc. The preparation of maps, GIS outputs and geo-statistical services can be included to maximise the value and capacity to analyse the statistical information. Methodological notes, to accompany the outputs and describe how they have been produced are also prepared in this sub-process taking as input the methodology designed in the Design phase. When new processing or analysis methods such as those based on machine learning or artificial intelligence are used, additional explanations might need to be prepared to communicate/explain the necessary information to the users.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The sub-process is now 'AI-powered pipelines. Outputs—including indices, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, geo-statistical services, write-ups, dashboards, and methodological documentation—are generated by default through LLM/AI-driven automation.' The 'Economist/Sociologist 2' ('participates in the analysis... and assists in the preparation of analytical material') is required to review, interpret, and contextualize automated outputs, ensure user-centric narrative, and tailor communication to nuanced or complex user needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer' ('edits, validates, markets and disseminates data', 'drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used') will increasingly focus on editing and validating automatically-produced analytical and narrative products, ensuring that AI-generated content is accessible, accurate, and suitable for intended audiences.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Validate outputs
description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Validation moves to 'automated, AI- and ML-powered, real-time digital workflows,' escalating only complex or unusual findings to human experts. The 'Economist/Sociologist 2', responsible for 'identifying statistical trends and developments' and 'participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on... editing, compilation and presentation methods,' will now focus on adjudicating anomalies, reviewing validation logic, and embedding domain intelligence into AI-supported validation processes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Data Production and Dissemination Officer', who 'reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases' and 'analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness,' will be responsible for interpreting and confirming automated QA outcomes, updating validation protocols, and supporting the refinement of machine-driven validation pipelines.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Interpret and explain outputs
description: This sub-process is where outputs are interpreted in order to understand their meaning and to try to explain them.
